liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (1 review): Reviewer thinks this Easy Wind is among the best the band ever played [14]
- **Ripple, take 1** (1 review): Reviewer defends the Ripple portion against complaints, and enjoys the false start [15]
- **Ripple** (1 review): Reviewer defends Ripple as a gem, one of the band's earliest recorded versions of the song, despite criticism [12]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Bird Song as a highlight of the new material [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **Where's Mickey Hart?**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]
- **Ripple, take 1**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [20]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.87134.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 27 songs; 166 min; rated 4.44/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes this soundboard as fantastic quality, intact and clear; Two anomalous frequency peaks, around 7-8K and 15.5-16.3K, appear throughout both sets and on earlier sources; Tape quality degrades around the reel flip during Wharf Rat [1][18]
- **gd71-02-21.sbd.lunz.1980.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 23 songs; 169 min; rated 4.27/5 by 15 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the soundboard ridiculously good, among the best heard on the site, and rejects an earlier negative review; Reviewer says Ripple sounds as though it comes from a different show than the rest of the recording; Reviewer finds the recording sounds pretty good, noting that listeners hear differently on different equipment [9][10][11][19]
- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.orf.98034.flac16**: soundboard; 23 songs; 169 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.miller.116618.flac16**: soundboard; 24 songs; 172 min; rated 3.82/5 by 11 [4]

## Around the show

- Attendee says this was the first show without Mickey, though his drums remained on stage [13]
- Attendee recalls long tuning, Phil spinning his cord, and Jerry bobbing, which later Deadheads may not know about [13]
- Reviewer notes the band adapted quickly to playing without Mickey [14]
- Reviewer finds the false start amusing, showing the band was still human [15]
- Reviewer says Capitol Theater shows are full of love, and even audience recordings from there are magical [16]
- Reviewer sees this show as a crossroads, with newer songs like Loser, Sugar Magnolia and Bird Song replacing the older Dark Star-Lovelight staples [9]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.cantor-crouch-diebert-gmb.87134.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Original WBOTB DATs procured & circulated in 1996 by Jace Crouch and Tim Deibert. Thanks to trailmix for providing the lineaged master DAT  for transfer.; transferred by Transfer and mastering by C.Ladner.; source: 7" two track BBD reel w/ Dolby A @ 7 1/2 ips > PCM501ES (beta) > PCM501ES analog out > Dolby A decoder > Apogee filter > analog in PCMF1/PCM501ES analog out >… [1]. Also: Each section was mastered with a separate Waves Q10 EQ setting, with supernotch on the affected frequencies [1]
- **gd71-02-21.sbd.lunz.1980.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Leigh Orf; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Chain: soundboard to Dolby A reel, Dolby A decode, DAT, Sound Forge noise reduction, then CD-R; Apparently sourced from the earlier Leigh Orf seed, with possible additions by Jason Lunz [2]
- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.orf.98034.flac16**: source: SBD -> Dobly A Reel -> Dolby A decode -> DAT -> Sound Forge NR -> CD-R; [3]. Also: Reviewer credits Leigh Orf for the mix, recording and transfer of this soundboard [16]
- **gd1971-02-21.sbd.miller.116618.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> CD [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by crepuscularthad.blogspot.com: [Brokedown Palace: The Capitol Theatre and the Grateful Dead](https://crepuscularthad.blogspot.com/2017/03/capitol-theatre-and-grateful-dead.html) [21]
